library.title: Maharashtra drought resilience: project priorities
library.summary: The shared mission, constraints and questions behind the field work.
body: The project aims to help farming families across Maharashtra manage water and fodder shortages through affordable practices they can maintain locally. Nashik is the starting location, with peer pilots and regional participation planned across the state.

The recorded priority is a complete, locally appropriate cattle-feeding approach, followed by safety and practical evidence for sprouted fodder. Crop-income and tower experiments remain separate candidates to evaluate with full water, labour and financial records.

Research notes contain candidate ideas and unresolved claims. They are not a finished animal-feeding protocol or evidence of a completed field trial. Qualified collaborators should review feeding changes for the animal and local ingredients.

library.title: How the hub treats evidence
library.summary: Dates, units, locations, source links and clear verification states.
body: Official observations, statistical estimates, forecasts, peer reports and modelled scenarios are separate record types. Every displayed value needs a location, date, unit, source and method.

A reservoir’s storage percentage is not a village supply estimate. Link the actual supply system, usable allocation, withdrawals and losses before estimating a shortage date. Leave estimates unavailable when the inputs are missing.

Census records and soil samples retain their reference dates. A peer’s local report remains a peer observation after review; it does not become an official reading. Household contact and financial information belongs in restricted records.

library.title: A common procedure for peer pilots
library.summary: A shared baseline, stable-method observations, repeated batches and honest failure records.
body: Assign a site ID, location code, responsible operator and protocol version. Record current practice before introducing the agreed change, and track observations in the same units across sites.

The proposed procedure uses a 14-day baseline and aims for 28 stable observation days after an appropriate adaptation period. A named qualified reviewer must accept any animal-feeding changes. Production experiments can be evaluated separately from household feeding.

Record all inputs, water including cleaning, labour, output, discarded batches and support time. Keep withdrawals and missing data in the final report. A small initial pilot does not establish performance throughout Maharashtra or in every season.

library.title: Micro-finance: full cost at each site
library.summary: Separate family cash, replacement value, programme costs and subsidy timing.
body: Record setup purchases, borrowed assets, donated materials and the family’s contribution separately. Routine costs include the whole feed or crop input bill, water, power, washing, losses, transport, repairs and local support.

Show actual receipts and avoided purchases without double-counting a saving already reflected in a lower expense. Value unpaid labour separately and include routine programme support when judging reproducibility.

Keep money received separate from applications and promised subsidies. Compute payback only from a positive observed incremental cash benefit, and disclose seasonal assumptions. No financial outcomes are established yet.

library.title: Spineless cactus: sourcing and local evaluation
library.summary: A possible longer-term fodder resource with sourcing, establishment and pest questions.
body: Existing research identifies BAIF and agricultural institutions as leads for fodder planting material. Availability, variety, price, transport and local suitability remain questions to confirm directly.

Local trials need to document establishment, drainage, pest incidence, water and labour before relying on harvest assumptions. Benefits seen in other species or climates should not be assumed for local cattle.
This brief provides research context, not a feeding recipe. Obtain qualified local advice before introducing a new feed.

library.title: Nashik fodder support: questions to verify
library.summary: A checklist for checking schemes, fodder banks, camps and local assistance.
body: The workspace research identifies possible fodder conservation and livestock-support programmes, but current local availability and scheme terms need original orders and implementing-office confirmation.

For each lead, confirm geography, eligible applicant, supported activity, application route, deadlines, required contribution, reimbursement timing and responsible contact. A news announcement does not establish an open application window.
Keep the original Marathi order and amendments alongside short summaries. Record what the local office confirms and the date; do not reuse historical camp rates as current benefits.

library.title: Tower designs and experimental growing systems
library.summary: Compare water delivery, maintenance, usable output and cost before selecting a system.
body: The workspace compares pocket towers, spray-cap columns and growing systems with media. An additional printable tower design includes downloaded parts, estimated material requirements and builder-reported watering and leakage issues.

The raw geometry report contains disputed measurements, so dimensional claims need reconciliation before design or manufacture. Material estimates do not represent a complete installed or operating price.
Compare candidate systems under documented local conditions using the same crop where practical. Record usable harvest, all direct water, labour, downtime, repairs and actual sale receipts.
